To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we used parallel ICA to investigate the genetic underpining of white matter integrity changes in SZ; 2) the identified FA-SNP component was overrepresented by genes whose products are associated with corpus callosum morphogenesis; 3) the SNP component was associated with decreased white matter integrity of the forceps major.

a multivariate approach was used to identify genetic markers of white matter abnormalities associated with schizophrenia, and that the identified genetic markers are overrepresented in genes involved in corpus callosal morphology, synaptic plasticity and protein kinase A pathway.

(1) a multivariate approach was applied to identify a genetic component associated with white matter abnormalities in schizophrenia; (2) the identified genetic component is involved in genes whose products play a role in neural development; and (3) the identified FA-SNP correlation was stable in a 73 SZ patients/87 HC cohort and a 10-fold cross-validation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for identifying the genetics of brain imaging phenotypes.
genetic factors associated with white matter integrity in patients with schizophrenia.
a novel multivariate analysis method, P-ICA, for genetic imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic architecture underlying white matter alterations in schizophrenia is complex, involving multiple genetic factors with modest effect sizes.
the genetic markers of white matter abnormalities identified in this study may be associated with the pathophysiology of SZ.
the identified genetic factor is a part of the genetic architecture underlying white matter integrity in SZ, and that it is associated with genes involved in neural development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P-ICA is an efficient approach to identify genetic markers of white matter abnormalities, which is potentially applicable to a wide range of neuroimaging studies.
genetic factors that contribute to SZ are also associated with white matter abnormalities.
the P-ICA framework is a useful tool in identifying genetic factors underlying neuroimaging phenotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multivariate approaches are powerful tools to investigate the complex genetic underpinnnings of brain disorders.
multivariate methods, such as P-ICA, can be useful to uncover the genetic basis of complex disorders, such as SZ.
the multivariate approach can effectively identify a set of genes with a modest individual effect size, which may not be detected by a single gene association analysis.
